headline: GOLD/SILVER BOUNCE FROM 7-MONTH LOWS — IRAN CEASEFIRE DROPS OIL, FED RATE-HIKE DOUBTS MOUNT
snippet: Gold and silver staged a meaningful Friday recovery from the 7-month lows hit earlier in the week, as two factors undermined the bear case: oil prices retreating to pre-Iran-conflict levels as the ceasefire holds — threatening to make May's 4.2% CPI print the inflation cycle peak — and growing market doubts that the Fed will follow through on the rate-hike scenario that drove the dollar to a 12-month high. Spot gold climbed toward $4,089–$4,165 on Friday, recovering from the sub-$4,000 breach seen earlier in the week, while silver reclaimed the $64–$65/oz range from a weekly low near $57–$59. BullionVault noted that robust central bank demand 'remains a critical pillar of support' even as speculative positioning unwound sharply during the post-FOMC selloff, while UBS flagged 'scope for renewed US dollar weakness.' The recovery narrative is important for junior mining investors: every major institutional gold target — Goldman $5,400, JPMorgan $6,000, UBS $5,500 — sits 25–44% above current prices, and the bull market's structural case (central bank buying, fiscal deficit trajectory, geopolitical risk) has not materially changed.

headline: WARSH KILLED THE FED'S RATE ROADMAP — WHAT THE MISSING DOT MEANS FOR GOLD AND SILVER
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues that the most consequential element of the June FOMC was not the nine of 18 members projecting a rate hike, but Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's decision to withhold his own rate projection from the dot plot entirely — without precedent in the dot plot's 14-year history. Rather than resolving uncertainty, the omission created a vacuum: the market has no authoritative Warsh signal, paradoxically producing more rate-path uncertainty than a hike would have. The analysis notes that silver fell from $69.85 to $64 in the FOMC week but recovered nearly 70% of that move, suggesting monetary-premium destruction has limits once the speculative unwind is complete. Historically, gold's most explosive rallies begin not when the Fed signals cuts, but when hawkish consensus is maximally priced-in — and the current $4,089–$4,165 spot price against institutional $5,200–$6,000 year-end targets represents the widest divergence in this bull cycle. The piece concludes that Warsh's omission leaves the Fed's next move entirely data-dependent, which, under an Iran ceasefire normalising oil prices, may mean rate hike odds fade faster than the market currently anticipates.

headline: SILVER ENTERING SIXTH STRAIGHT SUPPLY DEFICIT — 46.3 MOZ GAP IN 2026; THE CORRECTION WAS THE SETUP
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver price outlook argues that the 44% correction from January's historic $121/oz high has fully unwound the speculative excess of Q1, leaving silver's structural supply-demand fundamentals as the dominant pricing driver going forward. The global silver market is projected to register its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces in 2026 — wider than 2025 — despite a 19% reduction in solar photovoltaic silver demand as manufacturers adopted lower-intensity cell designs. AI data-centre infrastructure, EV electronics, and automotive applications are absorbing roughly two-thirds of solar's lost demand. Mine supply is contracting faster than industrial demand is falling, as capex cuts at primary copper and gold mines reduce byproduct silver output. The analysis targets a recovery toward $95–$106/oz by year-end 2026, contingent on the Fed rate-hike scare fading as oil normalises post-ceasefire. Note: China reclassified silver as a strategic material in January 2026, reducing the metal's ability to cushion paper-market selling with physical supply flows, which the piece considers a medium-term price support.

headline: GLOBAL URANIUM (CSE:GURN) DEPLOYS ANT SURVEY ON 25KM CONDUCTOR AT ATHABASCA'S ASTRO PROJECT
snippet: Global Uranium Corp. (CSE:GURN | OTC:GURFF) announced June 26 that an Ambient Noise Tomography survey has commenced at its Astro Project in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin, conducted by CAUR Technologies of Quebec. ANT delivers high-resolution shear wave velocity models to map lithological contrasts, structural features, and alteration zones at depth that conventional electromagnetic surveys cannot resolve alone — reducing first-drill targeting risk in a basin where holes can cost $500,000–$2M each depending on depth. The survey targets the AS-1 area, covering a significant portion of a 25-kilometre-long conductive corridor defined by Cosa Resources Corp.'s 2025 project-wide airborne survey — one of the longer untested conductive structures active in Athabasca exploration this season. Global Uranium holds an option to acquire up to 80% of Astro from Cosa Resources under an agreement announced April 9, 2025, and is fully funding this survey under its earn-in obligations. The Astro announcement is the third Athabasca Basin uranium exploration program initiation announced this week, reflecting intense summer-season activity across the basin as uranium spot prices hover near $85.85/lb.

headline: BANYAN GOLD FILES AURMAC TECHNICAL REPORT: 8.62 MOZ Au @ 0.62 g/t IN YUKON (TSXV:BYN)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV:BYN | OTC:BYAGF)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV:BYN | OTC:BYAGF) filed June 26 the NI 43-101 Technical Report supporting its updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the AurMac Project in the Traditional Territory of the First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun, Yukon — confirming 8.62 million ounces of gold at 0.62 g/t using a 0.3 g/t cut-off: 3.639 Moz Indicated at 0.68 g/t (167.3 Mt) and 4.985 Moz Inferred at 0.58 g/t (267.2 Mt), with an effective date of May 15, 2026. At this scale, AurMac ranks among the largest undeveloped open-pit gold resources in Canada by total ounces, positioned within the Tintina Gold Belt that hosts multi-million-ounce discoveries across Yukon and Alaska. The Technical Report was authored by Marc Jutras, P.Eng. (Ginto Consulting), Tysen Hantelmann, P.Eng. (JDS Energy & Mining), and Frank Wright, P.Eng. Filing the Technical Report clears the regulatory pathway for Banyan to advance to a Preliminary Economic Assessment — a milestone that becomes increasingly compelling as gold trades above $4,000/oz, well above the $3,000–$3,500 assumptions at which Yukon projects of this scale typically screen attractively.

headline: OMAI GOLD DRILLS 7.26 g/t AU OVER 34.8m AT WENOT, GUYANA — PEA 4-6 WEEKS OUT (TSXV:OMG)
source_name: Newsfile / Omai Gold Mines Corp. (TSXV:OMG | OTCQB:OMGGF)
snippet: Omai Gold Mines Corp. (TSXV:OMG | OTCQB:OMGGF) reported June 24 assay results from six additional diamond drill holes at its 100%-owned Omai Gold Project in Guyana, with highlight hole 26ODD-185 returning 7.26 g/t gold over 34.8 metres from 200 metres depth — one of 15 discrete gold-mineralised intervals intersected in that single hole. Five drill rigs continue operating on-site, with 58 holes totalling 27,770 metres of the planned 50,000-metre 2026 program now complete. Phase 1 metallurgical results released June 22 confirmed 93–95% gold recoveries at both the Wenot and Gilt deposits using a standard carbon-in-leach circuit with a 32-hour retention time, eliminating a key technical risk ahead of the Preliminary Economic Assessment that Omai expects to deliver within 4–6 weeks — placing an Omai PEA firmly in Q3 2026. The project is located at the site of Cambior Inc.'s former Omai Mine, which produced approximately 3.7 million ounces of gold before closure in 2005, providing strong geological context for current resource growth. Guyana has attracted significant investment capital following ExxonMobil's offshore discoveries and the government's push to develop interior mineral resources.

headline: NEWCORE GOLD ENCHI PFS: $496M NPV, 37% IRR — GHANA MINING LEASE APPLICATION IN 2026 (TSXV:NCAU)
snippet: Newcore Gold Ltd. (TSXV:NCAU | OTCQX:NCAUF) announced June 24 the Pre-Feasibility Study for its Enchi Gold Project in southwest Ghana — a conventional open-pit, carbon-in-leach operation processing 5.5 million tonnes per annum on contract mining over a 24-month construction period. At a conservative US$3,800/oz base case (approximately $300/oz below current spot), Enchi returns an after-tax NPV5% of US$496 million, an IRR of 37%, and requires US$351 million in upfront capital. The 248 km² property covers approximately 40 kilometres of the Bibiani Shear Zone — the same trend hosting Newmont's Ahafo Mine and Asante Gold's Bibiani and Chirano operations. Newcore plans to file a mining lease application in Ghana in 2026 based on the PFS. Mixed market reaction: The Northern Miner headlined its coverage 'Newcore Gold tanks as Enchi prefeasibility disappoints,' suggesting the $351M capex or timeline exceeded some pre-study analyst expectations, despite the project delivering a solid 37% IRR at conservative gold price assumptions that look increasingly conservative given current market pricing.

headline: FARADAY COPPER (LUNDIN) HITS 73m AT 0.31% CU FROM SURFACE AT AMERICAN EAGLE, ARIZONA (TSX:FDY)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY)
snippet: Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY), a Lundin Group company advancing the Copper Creek porphyry project in Arizona, announced June 24 results from 18 Phase IV drill holes, with five holes in the American Eagle area demonstrating near-surface copper mineralisation that materially improves the open-pit economic scenario. Highlight hole FCD-26-173 returned 73 metres at 0.31% copper from surface, including 37 metres at 0.45% from 20 metres depth; FCD-26-169 returned 67 metres at 0.30% from 30 metres; FCD-26-171 returned 71 metres at 0.41% from 80 metres. Near-surface oxide and oxide-transition mineralisation at Copper Creek can potentially be heap-leached at significantly lower capital cost than milling deeper porphyry material — strategically important given the pending June 30 US Section 232 copper tariff decision, under which domestically-produced US copper would command a structural pricing premium. Faraday paused drilling on June 20 pending the proposed San Manuel Property acquisition; drilling is expected to resume in fall 2026 once the acquisition closes.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS ADDS THIRD DRILL RIG AT ML PROJECT, YUKON — EXPANDED PROGRAM UNDERWAY (TSXV:PPP)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV:PPP)
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV:PPP) provided a June 25 drilling update confirming that a third diamond drill rig was expected to arrive at the ML Project in Yukon's Dawson Range on June 27, expanding the active drill count to three. Three-rig programs in the Yukon junior exploration sector are capital-intensive commitments that operators typically make only when early-hole results justify accelerated step-out and infill work — the acceleration here is a signal, not a routine logistics update. The ML Project is a developing gold target within the Dawson Range, a district hosting several well-established Yukon gold systems. No assay results from the 2026 program have yet been released; a batch of results from expanded drilling would likely represent a catalytic news event. With gold holding above $4,000/oz even through its worst weekly correction of 2026, Yukon exploration-stage companies with active drill programs occupy an unusually attractive risk/reward position against historical discovery valuations.

headline: MORGAN STANLEY: GOLD DOWN 25% BUT ONE CPI NUMBER UNLOCKS $5,200 TARGET — ETF FLOWS THE KEY
snippet: GoldSilver.com's synthesis of Morgan Stanley's revised H2 2026 gold framework identifies institutional ETF inflows as the single variable separating current gold prices (~$4,165, down 25% from January's $5,589 ATH) from the bank's $5,200 year-end target. Morgan Stanley's model holds that structural central bank buying sustains the floor, but a reacceleration to new highs requires institutional investors — who have been net sellers since January — to re-engage via gold ETFs. The trigger for that rotation: a CPI print that convincingly removes the December Fed rate-hike scenario (currently 80% priced by CME FedWatch). With oil retreating to pre-Iran-conflict levels as the ceasefire holds, the May 4.2% CPI may represent the inflation cycle peak — and a lower-than-expected June or July CPI reading would constitute exactly the institutional re-entry catalyst Morgan Stanley's framework requires. All major institutional year-end gold forecasts — Goldman Sachs $5,400, JPMorgan $6,000, UBS $5,500, Morgan Stanley $5,200 — sit 25–44% above current levels, the widest consensus-vs-spot divergence of the 2025–2026 bull cycle.

headline: LITHIUM CLIMBS ABOVE $21/KG NE ASIA — ENERGY STORAGE ACCOUNTS FOR 31% OF GLOBAL DEMAND IN 2026
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate prices in Northeast Asia climbed above $21.38/kg in June 2026 (up 0.4%), with Chinese domestic prices rising to CNY 169,000/tonne from a near two-month low of CNY 163,000 as seasonal inventory rebuilding triggered renewed buying. The recovery follows Q1 2026's sharp rally that took battery-grade lithium carbonate to US$26,278/tonne before a partial Q2 correction. The structural demand driver is stationary energy storage: lithium demand from grid and behind-the-meter storage systems jumped 71% in 2025 and is forecast to grow another 55% in 2026, bringing energy storage's share of total lithium carbonate equivalent demand to 31% from 23% a year ago — a structural shift that partially insulates the market from year-over-year swings in EV production growth. Chinese lepidolite mine supply has tightened due to operational halts tied to licence renewals at Yichun-area mines, underpinning prices. Analysts at Morgan Stanley and UBS have revised supply models toward a deficit for H2 2026. Junior lithium explorers in Canada (Yukon, Ontario, Quebec) and Australia (Western Australia, South Australia) remain the primary vehicle for retail investors seeking leveraged exposure to a price recovery from below-incentive levels.
